prompt: Apple Computer was founded
explanation: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne founded Apple Computer, helping launch the personal-computer era.

prompt: The Apple II went on sale
explanation: The Apple II became one of the first highly successful mass-produced personal computers.

prompt: The first widely recognized spam email was sent on ARPANET
explanation: A marketing message for DEC computers sent to hundreds of ARPANET users is widely cited as the first commercial spam email.

prompt: Usenet was created
explanation: Usenet introduced distributed discussion groups years before the public web and became an early home for online communities.

prompt: CompuServe launched its CB Simulator online chat service
explanation: CB Simulator brought real-time multi-user text chat to a large commercial online audience.

prompt: IBM launched the IBM Personal Computer
explanation: The IBM PC helped establish the hardware and software conventions that shaped the personal-computer market.

prompt: The :-) emoticon was proposed for online messages
explanation: Scott Fahlman proposed :-) and :-( on a Carnegie Mellon message board to distinguish jokes from serious posts.

prompt: ARPANET switched to TCP/IP
explanation: The January 1 transition to TCP/IP is one of the foundational milestones in the emergence of the modern Internet.

prompt: The Domain Name System was introduced
explanation: DNS replaced an increasingly unmanageable central host list with the distributed naming system still used on the Internet today.

prompt: Symbolics.com became the first registered .com domain
explanation: Symbolics.com is recognized as the first domain registered under the .com top-level domain.

prompt: NSFNET began building a major Internet backbone
explanation: The National Science Foundation network connected research centers and became a crucial backbone for the growing Internet.

prompt: CompuServe introduced the GIF image format
explanation: GIF became one of the web’s defining image formats and later a core part of online reaction culture.

prompt: The Morris worm disrupted thousands of Internet-connected computers
explanation: The Morris worm was one of the first major Internet worms and helped push computer security into the mainstream.

prompt: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web at CERN
explanation: Berners-Lee’s proposal described a hypertext system for sharing information across networked computers at CERN.

prompt: ARPANET was decommissioned
explanation: By the time ARPANET shut down, TCP/IP-based networks had grown far beyond the original research network.

prompt: CERN opened the World Wide Web to the public
explanation: The first web software was made available outside CERN, beginning the web’s spread beyond its research origins.

prompt: The first photograph was published on the World Wide Web
explanation: A photo of the CERN parody band Les Horribles Cernettes became an early landmark in visual web culture.

prompt: The Mosaic web browser was released
explanation: Mosaic made the web dramatically easier to use and helped popularize graphical browsing.

prompt: Yahoo! began as a hand-built directory of the web
explanation: Jerry Yang and David Filo created a directory of websites that evolved into Yahoo!, one of the early web’s defining portals.

prompt: Amazon sold its first book online
explanation: Amazon began as an online bookstore before expanding into one of the world’s largest ecommerce and cloud companies.

prompt: Hotmail launched as one of the first major webmail services
explanation: Hotmail helped popularize the idea that email could be accessed from any web browser instead of a single computer.

prompt: Netflix was founded
explanation: Netflix began as a DVD-by-mail company before becoming a defining streaming platform.

prompt: Google was founded
explanation: Larry Page and Sergey Brin incorporated Google after developing a search engine based on links between web pages.

prompt: Napster launched and changed music sharing forever
explanation: Napster made peer-to-peer music sharing mainstream and forced the music industry to confront digital distribution.

prompt: Google launched AdWords
explanation: AdWords created the advertising engine that would become central to Google’s business model and the wider web economy.

prompt: Wikipedia launched
explanation: Wikipedia turned collaborative editing into one of the largest reference works ever created.

prompt: Friendster launched
explanation: Friendster was one of the first social networks to reach a mass audience before MySpace and Facebook overtook it.

prompt: MySpace launched
explanation: MySpace became a major center of music, identity and online social life during the mid-2000s.

prompt: Facebook launched from a Harvard dorm
explanation: TheFacebook launched for Harvard students before expanding across universities and eventually the world.

prompt: The first video was uploaded to YouTube
explanation: Jawed Karim uploaded “Me at the zoo,” the first video on a platform that would reshape online video and creator culture.

prompt: Twitter launched
explanation: Twitter introduced a public short-message network that became central to real-time news, culture and online conversation.

prompt: Steve Jobs unveiled the first iPhone
explanation: The iPhone combined a phone, widescreen iPod and web-capable mobile device, accelerating the shift to the mobile Internet.

prompt: The Bitcoin white paper was published
explanation: The paper titled “Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System” proposed a decentralized digital currency using a blockchain.

prompt: WhatsApp launched
explanation: WhatsApp grew from a simple status app into one of the world’s most widely used private messaging services.

prompt: Instagram launched
explanation: Instagram made mobile photo sharing a mainstream social behavior and rapidly grew into a major visual platform.

prompt: Snapchat launched
explanation: Snapchat popularized disappearing messages and later helped make vertical, camera-first social media mainstream.

prompt: “Gangnam Style” became the first YouTube video to hit one billion views
explanation: PSY’s viral hit became the first YouTube video to cross one billion views, a milestone for global online culture.

prompt: Vine launched its six-second looping videos
explanation: Vine compressed video creativity into six-second loops and became a breeding ground for a new generation of online creators.

prompt: The Ice Bucket Challenge flooded social feeds around the world
explanation: The viral challenge showed how social media could turn a simple participatory format into global fundraising and awareness.

prompt: Discord launched
explanation: Discord began as a voice and text chat tool for gamers and grew into a broader platform for online communities.

prompt: Pokémon GO sent millions of players outside with their phones
explanation: Pokémon GO combined mobile gaming, maps and augmented reality into a global location-based phenomenon.

prompt: Fortnite Battle Royale launched
explanation: Fortnite Battle Royale became a huge free-to-play hit and a major social space for gaming, streaming and virtual events.

prompt: TikTok became a global app after merging with Musical.ly
explanation: The merger consolidated TikTok’s short-form video product and audience, accelerating its global rise.

prompt: Disney+ launched
explanation: Disney entered the direct-to-consumer streaming race with a service built around Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars and more.

prompt: OpenAI introduced GPT-3
explanation: GPT-3 demonstrated that scaling language models could produce surprisingly broad few-shot and zero-shot capabilities.

prompt: Wordle was released to the public
explanation: Josh Wardle’s simple once-a-day word game became a viral ritual built around scarcity, sharing and social comparison.

prompt: ChatGPT launched
explanation: OpenAI released ChatGPT as a research preview, bringing conversational generative AI to a mass audience.

prompt: Threads launched as Meta’s text-first social app
explanation: Meta launched Threads as an Instagram-linked app for public text conversation during a period of major change at Twitter/X.

prompt: Apple Vision Pro went on sale
explanation: Apple’s first spatial computer reached customers in the United States, marking its biggest new hardware category in years.
